MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center

PATIENT: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
SEX: Male
ORDERING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE OF COLLECTION: [redacted date]
DATE OF REPORT: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
BRAF mutation analysis requested for therapeutic decision-making in patient with suspected BRAF-associated malignancy.

SPECIMEN
Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue
Neoplastic cell content: 80%

METHODOLOGY
Targeted Sanger sequencing of BRAF exon 15 was performed following PCR amplification of DNA extracted from FFPE tissue. The assay specifically interrogates codon 600 and surrounding regions for activating variants. DNA was extracted using the QIAamp DNA FFPE Tissue Kit (Qiagen). PCR amplification was performed using primers flanking BRAF exon 15, followed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing on an Applied Biosystems 3730xl DNA Analyzer.

Analytical sensitivity: This assay can reliably detect the c.1799T>A p.(Val600Glu) variant at a minimum variant allele frequency of 20% in samples with adequate neoplastic cell content.

RESULTS

Gene: BRAF (NM_004333.6)
Exon analyzed: Exon 15
Codon 600 status: Wild-type

No activating BRAF variant detected in exon 15.

Note: This assay has a detection sensitivity of 20% for the c.1799T>A p.(Val600Glu) variant. Variants present below this threshold cannot be excluded.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The absence of detectable BRAF exon 15 activating mutations suggests this patient is unlikely to benefit from BRAF/MEK-targeted therapy. BRAF V600 mutations are actionable alterations in multiple cancer types including melanoma, colorectal carcinoma, and other malignancies. The wild-type BRAF status indicates that alternative therapeutic strategies should be considered.

LIMITATIONS
- This assay is limited to BRAF exon 15 and does not detect variants in other exons
- Variants present at allele frequencies below 20% may not be detected
- Rare variants outside the primer binding sites will not be amplified

REFERENCES
1. Davies H, et al. Mutations of the BRAF gene in human cancer. Nature. 2002;417(6892):949-54.
2. Chapman PB, et al. Improved survival with vemurafenib in melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation. N Engl J Med. 2011;364(26):2507-16.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Molecular Pathologist
[redacted date]
